title: A Durable Object migration declared out of tag order never runs
description:
Deploying the factory from epic/dha on 2026-09-20 failed:

    Cannot create binding for class 'RepoRoom' because it is not currently
    configured to implement Durable Objects. Configure a migration in your
    configuration to add this class. [code: 10061]

The migration WAS declared. cloudflare/wrangler.toml had its [[migrations]] blocks written next to the bindings they belong to, which put the tags out of order in the file:

    line 22  tag v1  RunRoom
    line 37  tag v4  RepoRoom     <- out of place
    line 63  tag v2  Sandbox
    line 67  tag v3  SignalInbox

wrangler applies migrations in FILE ORDER, continuing after the last tag the deployed worker already applied. A worker at v3 sees nothing after v3 in the file, so RepoRoom's migration never ran, and the API then refused the binding for a class it was never told to create.

Fixed by moving the v4 block below v3, with a comment saying why it cannot live beside its binding. Tags must ascend down the file.

This is why Phase 4's factory could not deploy from a branch carrying ef7's RepoRoom. Nobody noticed because nobody deployed it - which is exactly the gap u9h exists to close.

A guard is worth having: a test that reads wrangler.toml and refuses tags that do not ascend would have caught this at gate time rather than at deploy time.
acceptance_criteria: A test refuses a wrangler.toml whose [[migrations]] tags do not ascend in file order, and fails on the pre-fix file
